text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 billing persists across every complexity stratum, including many visits for patients with no or one chronic condition, but documentation is too thin to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern raises concern because the excess 99215 share is not confined to sicker patients. It appears in every complexity band, and the gap relative to peers is largest for patients with zero or one chronic condition. Sampled low-complexity 99215 claims such as C0076994, C0077539 and C0077894 (J06.9 only) and C0077102 (N39.0 only) carry diagnoses that would not usually support high-complexity MDM. The rule check found too few documented claims to lean either way. The 2 of 5 documented 99215s recorded at moderate MDM (C0076995, C0077137) are suggestive, but five charts cannot separate upcoding from documentation noise. Likewise, the single moderate-plus data-reviewed note without a lab line is weak evidence at most. A reviewer should first pull charts for a larger sample of 99215 claims, prioritizing the 0–1 condition visits listed here, and check whether MDM or time actually supports level 5."}
